title: epan: apply endianness fixes
description:
Historically a boolean (TRUE/FALSE) was being used for little/big
endian encoding designation. With the introduction of the encoding
enum, for backward compatibility reasons, the boolean interpretation
of this encoding designation is supported to determine endianness.
This leads to a lot of code using ENC_NA where ENC_BIG_ENDIAN is
intended, because these 'promote' to the same boolean interpretation.

With this commit a series of identified incorrect endianness
designations are corrected. A few other endianness related are issues
are addressed as well.

notes.body:
In this case, `cigi_byte_order` is either `ENC_BIG_ENDIAN` or `ENC_LITTLE_ENDIAN`, so comparing it with `ENC_BIG_ENDIAN` suffices (and may generate slightly less machine code, testing the value against 0).

If we're going to test whether the `ENC_LITTLE_ENDIAN` is set, rather than whether it's equal to `ENC_BIG_ENDIAN`, we should probably reverse the true and false arms of the if, so that the test is `if (cigi_byte_order & ENC_LITTLE_ENDIAN) {`, making it a bit clearer that the first arm of the if is for little-endian byte order.

> ... so comparing it with `ENC_BIG_ENDIAN` suffices (and may generate slightly less machine code, testing the value against 0).

This assuming ENC_BIG_ENDIAN is always going to be '0x00000000'.

> ... we should probably reverse the true and false arms of the if, so that ...

To not overload the already rather large change with optimizations besides the critical parts (i.e., the selection logic) of the changes, I opted to leave them out.
